title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: Any $n$-vertex graph with fewer than $3n-6$ edges admits a bipartite cut, while some graphs with $3n-6$ edges do not. In particular, $\ell_{3}=3$.
context_text: The case $k=3$ was investigated by Bogdanov, Neustroeva, Sokolov, Volostnov, Russkin, and Voronov, who formulated this conjecture. The extremal examples are provided by $3$-trees. Partial progress on related statements (forest cuts and bipartite cuts) was obtained in the same work and subsequently by Botler et al. and Cheng, Tang and Zhan.
attributed_to: Bogdanov, Neustroeva, Sokolov, Volostnov, Russkin, and Voronov
paper_contribution: The paper does not directly prove or disprove Conjecture 1.2; it cites it as motivation for the general Conjecture 1.3, which the paper refutes for all sufficiently large $k$, showing that $\ell_k \sim \frac{k}{2}$ rather than $\ell_k = k$.
paper_title: On cuts of small chromatic number in sparse graphs

title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: For every integer $k$ and every graph $G$ on at least $k$ vertices, if $$|E(G)|<k|V(G)|-\tfrac{k(k+1)}{2},$$ then $G$ admits a cut $X$ with $\chi(G[X])<k$. In particular, $\ell_{k}=k$.
context_text: A cut (or separator) of a graph $G$ is a set $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $G\setminus X$ is disconnected. For an integer $k$, $\ell_k$ is the supremum of the reals $\ell$ such that every sufficiently large graph (as a function of $k$ and $\ell$) with average degree less than $2\ell$ has a cut $X$ with $\chi(G[X])<k$. A minimum-degree argument gives $\ell_k\ge k/2$, and joining a $k$-clique completely to an independent set of size $n-k$ gives an $n$-vertex graph with exactly $kn-\frac{k(k+1)}{2}$ edges in which every cut contains the clique, so $\ell_k\le k$; the conjectured edge bound is exactly the one of this example. It is folklore that $\ell_1=1$; Chen and Yu proved that every $n$-vertex graph with fewer than $2n-3$ edges has a stable cut, so $\ell_2=2$; Bogdanov et al. conjectured that fewer than $3n-6$ edges forces a bipartite cut ($\ell_3=3$). This conjecture is the natural generalization formulated by the authors, whose main purpose is to show that it is far from correct: they prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $k$, $\ell_k\le(1+\varepsilon)\frac{k}{2}$, so $\ell_k\sim k/2$, and indeed that there are arbitrarily large graphs of average degree $(1+o(1))k$ in which every cut contains a $k$-clique (which also rules out the stronger version asking for a $(k-2)$-degenerate cut). They ask for the smallest $k$ for which the conjecture fails, in particular whether it already fails for $k=3$.
notes: This conjecture is introduced by the paper's own authors and immediately refuted within the same paper: Theorem 1.4 shows $\ell_k \leq (1+\varepsilon)\frac{k}{2}$ for all sufficiently large $k$, so that asymptotically $\ell_k \sim \frac{k}{2}$ rather than $\ell_k = k$.
paper_title: On cuts of small chromatic number in sparse graphs
